title: When Part of a Host's Deductible is Given Back
content:
Part of the deductible a host carries against their Keyturn Host Payout Account is given back where the marketplace has recovered money under the host's Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment. What is given back is a share of the deductible the host carries, and the part given back is rounded half to even to two decimal places before it is taken off.

| Finding on the loss | Money recovered under the enrolment | Share of the deductible given back |
|---|---|---|
| The loss was found to be the guest's fault | Yes | 50 percent |
| The loss was found to be a third party's fault, or no one's fault | Yes | 25 percent |
| Any other case | Any | 0 percent |

## Both parts of each row

Each of the first two rows requires both a finding and a recovery. Where the loss was found to be the guest's fault but nothing has been recovered under the enrolment, neither of the first two rows is met and the third governs, so none of the deductible is given back. Where money has been recovered under the enrolment but the finding on the loss is neither of those named, the third row governs likewise.

## Cases on hypothetical figures

On a hypothetical deductible carried of 800.00 USD, where the loss was found to be the guest's fault and money has been recovered under the enrolment, 400.00 USD is given back and the deductible payable is 400.00 USD. On the same carried deductible, where the loss was found to be a third party's fault and money has been recovered, 200.00 USD is given back and the deductible payable is 600.00 USD. Where neither row is met, nothing is given back and the deductible payable is the whole 800.00 USD.

The finding is the one carried on the most recent appraisal made under the enrolment, and whether money has been recovered is read from the recovery entries standing against that same enrolment; both sit in the claim records of the Keyturn Host Protection Plan.
